sections.h2: Where is Carson City and what is the terrain like?
sections.html:
Carson City is Nevada's capital, in Eagle Valley on the eastern edge of the Carson Range of the Sierra Nevada, about 30 miles south of Reno. Its elevation is about 4,682 feet.

The city's total area is 157.12 square miles, of which 144.53 square miles is land. The boundary runs west across the Sierra Nevada to the California-Nevada state line in the middle of Lake Tahoe, so a Carson City address can mean a valley floor lot, a foothill lot with a view and mountain terrain. Slope, access roads and nearby open land all shape what a buyer will ask about.

The Census Bureau estimates 58,571 residents as of July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: What is the history of Carson City?
sections.html:
Carson City was founded in 1858 after Abraham Curry bought Eagle Station, and it was incorporated in 1875.

It has served as the capital since 1861, when Nevada was still a territory, and was confirmed as the permanent state capital in 1864. The Carson City Mint operated from 1870 to 1893. An older house may have original wiring, plumbing and foundations that a buyer will want inspected.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Carson City?
sections.html:
State agencies, the school district, a community college, retailers and casinos make up the largest employers in Carson City.

Wikipedia's employer list puts the Carson City School District in the 1,000 to 1,499 employee range. The Nevada Department of Transportation and Western Nevada College each employ 500 to 999 people. Between 200 and 499 employees each are the Nevada Department of Corrections, the Department of Motor Vehicles, Casino Fandango, Walmart, Precision Castparts, Gold Dust West, the Carson Nugget, Costco and the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

Owners who change jobs or retire sometimes need to sell without a long listing period.

sections.h2: What is the Carson City climate, and what does it mean for a roof and heating?
sections.html:
Carson City has a cold semi-arid climate with cold winters and hot summers, and 125 mornings a year start below freezing.

The average annual snowfall is 14.0 inches and the average annual precipitation is 9.34 inches, with most of it falling in winter and spring. The July average daily high is 89.5 degrees Fahrenheit, and about 39.5 afternoons a year reach 90 degrees or more. Freezing nights stress water pipes, exposed hose bibs and roofs with poor insulation, so a buyer's inspector will pay attention to heating systems, attic insulation and plumbing in unheated crawl spaces.

  • Water heater and furnace age.
  • Roof condition after snow loads.
  • Exterior pipes and sprinkler systems that need winterizing.

sections.h2: Is wildfire a concern for Carson City homes?
sections.html:
Yes, the city's own Community Wildfire Protection Plan identifies 25 high-priority sites with risk scores, so wildfire is a documented concern.

The plan describes a city of roughly 100,600 acres. The highest-scoring site on its list is Clear Creek in the southwest, followed by Timberline and Lakeview in the northwest and Mexican Dam in the southeast. Past fires it records include the Kings Canyon Fire in August 1988 at 1,798 acres, the Waterfall Fire in July 2004 at 8,764 acres, which destroyed several structures and vehicles, and the Prison Hill fire in July 2021 at 171 acres.

If your home is on the edge of open land, tell buyers about any defensible space work you have done. Ask your insurance agent about coverage early, so a buyer's lender does not raise it late.

sections.h2: Which highways and school district serve Carson City?
sections.html:
US 395, US 50, Interstate 580 and Nevada State Route 28 are the main routes, and the Carson City School District serves the city.

Buyers weigh these connections, so say how long the drive to Reno or to the Capitol complex actually takes from your address.

sections.h2: What disclosures and transfer tax apply when selling in Carson City?
sections.html:
A Carson City seller must complete Nevada's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form under NRS 113.130, and the state transfer tax is $1.95 per $500 of value.

The state's transfer tax page lists $1.95 for every $500 of value for all counties, with extra amounts only for Washoe, Churchill and Clark counties. Carson City is not among those, so the base rate is the one the page shows. Confirm the final figure with the recorder or your title company before closing. A declaration of value must accompany each deed presented for recording, and NRS 375 allows the tax to be collected from either the buyer or the seller.

Nevada's residential guide notes that a buyer who closes without a completed disclosure, or without being told of a known defect, may be entitled to treble damages unless the buyer waives that right. Disclose known problems, including roof leaks, water damage and past fire damage.

sections.h2: How are Carson City property taxes billed, and what are the dates?
sections.html:
The Carson City Treasurer mails real property tax bills in mid-July for the fiscal year starting July 1, and taxes can be paid in four installments.

For the 2026-2027 tax year the Treasurer lists the due dates as Monday, August 17, 2026, Monday, October 5, 2026, Monday, January 4, 2027 and Monday, March 1, 2027. The tax rate is set around the end of June and applied to values the Assessor sets as of June 30. A first late installment carries a 4 percent penalty, and parcels with taxes still due at the end of April are advertised as delinquent in the local newspaper.

InstallmentDue date, 2026-2027

State law gives owner-occupants of a single-family primary residence a partial abatement that limits the yearly increase in the tax bill to about 3 percent. The statute, NRS 361.4723, excludes homes rented to people other than the owner and the owner's family.

sections.h2: Are short-term rentals changing in Carson City?
sections.html:
Carson City supervisors moved toward a short-term rental licensing ordinance in 2026, but we could not confirm its final adoption.

The Nevada Appeal reported that on August 6, 2026 the Board of Supervisors unanimously approved the first reading. The proposal covers rentals of 28 days or less, calls for a $500 business license and a $25 application fee, allows one short-term rental per property, requires a maintenance log and bear-proof containers, and would take effect November 1. It would not apply to residents who rent a room or two. A second reading was still needed. If you are selling a house that has been used as a rental, ask the city what rules apply to it now.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Carson City?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so closing does not depend on loan approval or an appraisal.

You still complete the disclosure form, clear title, pay off any mortgage or lien at closing and sign a deed that goes to the county recorder with a declaration of value. Cash Home Buyers reviews the house as it is, makes no promise on price in advance, and you can turn down an offer with no cost to you. Sellers dealing with an inherited house, deferred repairs or a tenant often find this route more practical than preparing a listing.

faqs.q: How far is Carson City from Reno?
faqs.a: Carson City is about 30 miles south of Reno, in Eagle Valley at the foot of the Carson Range of the Sierra Nevada.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Carson City?
faqs.a: The state's page lists $1.95 per $500 of value for all counties, with add-ons only for Washoe, Churchill and Clark. Verify the figure with your title company, since the contract decides which party pays.

faqs.q: When are Carson City property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due on the third Monday of August, with installments on the first Mondays of October, January and March. In 2026-2027 those dates are August 17, October 5, January 4 and March 1.

faqs.q: Is Carson City at risk of wildfire?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Community Wildfire Protection Plan ranks 25 high-priority sites and lists past fires, including the 8,764-acre Waterfall Fire in July 2004.

faqs.q: Do I need a short-term rental license in Carson City?
faqs.a: A proposed ordinance would require a $500 business license, but we could not confirm it was finally adopted. Check with Carson City directly before relying on either answer.
